name: uas-sort (minimal): one WPF window over a pure UasSort.Core library
summary: You start uas-sort yourself; it opens a single window. It scans one DJI card and lists the video and photo roots by name, size and modified time only, so it never opens OneDrive placeholder files. It proposes video folders by grouping clips on the local date where they were shot (consecutive days join, G = 1) and on GPS: a clip more than R = 25 km from its group's centre starts a new group, even on the same day or the next day. To answer the request directly: yes, the photos' EXIF has coordinates (PANO_0001.DNG = 57.799648, -152.390180, read with MetadataExtractor), and every MP4 carries GPS in its djmd telemetry track, read by a small first-sample reader (about 300 lines of our own code). Drone-clock times (US Eastern) are converted to UTC using an offset learned from each MP4's true-UTC creation time, then to the local date of the shoot site with GeoTimeZone. The user edits descriptions, merges or splits groups, and chooses between appending to an existing folder and creating a new one. The app then copies, never writing to the card, checks every copy by re-reading it with SHA-256, and adds one line per checked file to a JSONL ledger. It uses only two runtime NuGet packages (MetadataExtractor, GeoTimeZone). Everything optional is cut. I re-ran the replay of the real library with the simplified grouping rules this design uses (time plus radius only; no power-on-session or re-homing logic). It still recreates all 8 of your folders, with the same safe ranges as the full design (R 12.5 to 53 km, G 1 to 11 days). The append-or-new-folder scenarios B to E also come out the same as the full reference.
stack: .NET 10 LTS. SDK 10.0.401 must be installed on Windows first; the machine currently has only SDK 9.0.316, and .NET 8 and 9 end support on 2026-11-10. VS 2022 cannot target net10, so use the dotnet CLI or VS Code. Solution C:\dev\uas-sort\uas-sort.sln, three projects: (1) UasSort.Core, net10.0 class library with no UI and no Windows APIs apart from one optional flag in RealFileOps; (2) UasSort.App, net10.0-windows WPF (UseWPF=true), published as a framework-dependent single-file win-x64 exe (about 4.9 MB measured; needs the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime); (3) UasSort.Core.Tests, xUnit plus Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk (test-only; versions pinned at scaffold time, UNVERIFIED). The tests run on Windows dotnet and in WSL with a Linux .NET 10 SDK. Runtime NuGet packages, only two: MetadataExtractor 2.9.3 (Apache-2.0; still-image EXIF) and GeoTimeZone 6.1.0 (MIT; latitude/longitude to IANA zone, 3.5 MB). Built-in APIs cover the rest: System.Text.Json for settings and ledger, IncrementalHash SHA-256 for verification (2 GB/s, far faster than any SD card), TimeZoneInfo.FindSystemTimeZoneById with IANA IDs (works on Windows 11 through ICU; do not enable InvariantGlobalization or UseNls), DriveInfo, and the WPF DataGrid and Expander. No MVVM toolkit (a hand-written ObservableObject and RelayCommand of about 40 lines), no SQLite, no System.IO.Hashing, no ExifTool, no WinUI or Avalonia.

components.name: Core/Io: IFileOps + GuardedFileOps + RealFileOps
components.responsibility: The only I/O surface in the app, and the place where the safety rules are enforced. It enforces three rules. (a) Library files (under the video root or photo root) are never opened for reading, except our own *.uas-sort.tmp files. This protects OneDrive placeholders from being downloaded. (b) Nothing is ever written, moved or deleted under the card root. (c) Only our own *.uas-sort.tmp files are ever deleted. Listing uses directory enumeration only, which returns size and modified time without opening files; the grouping spike's stat pass over the library left all 30 cloud-only Kodiak files cloud-only (0x401620). RealFileOps.OpenVerify opens with FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING ((FileOptions)0x20000000, 4096-aligned buffer) and falls back to a buffered read if that fails.

components.name: Core/Metadata: Mp4Probe (own code, no dependency)
components.responsibility: A C# port of spikes/djmd/djmd_gps.py with the optional parts removed. It walks the top-level MP4 boxes lazily: 8 or 16-byte headers, a size of 0 means the box runs to end of file, and neither the mdat box nor the whole moov box is ever read. It returns HasMoov (false means a truncated recording). From mvhd it reads the creation time: seconds since 1904, version 0 or 1, true UTC on DJI. It finds the track whose stsd entry is 'djmd' and keeps stsc in memory. It reads stsz, stco and co64 entries one at a time by seeking. It decodes protobuf generically (varint, fixed64, length-delimited). GPS is at path 3-3-4-1, in radians unless field 1 of the GPSInfo message is 1. It reads sample 0; if that has no fix (|lat| and |lon| below 1e-6), it tries the last sample, which is 2 reads at most. The spike read about 2 KB in 3–16 ms per file, versus 7–87 s for exiftool -ee3.

components.name: Core/Time: DroneClock + TimeResolver + ISiteZone
components.responsibility:
Turns every item into a CaptureUtc and a LocalDate at the shoot site. DroneClock collects samples from each DJI MP4 that has a moov: (filename stamp, filename stamp minus mvhd UTC, rounded to 15 minutes). For a photo, set or truncated clip it uses the offset of the nearest sample within 60 days. Otherwise it falls back to Settings.DroneClockOffsetMinutes, which is saved from the last learned value (currently -240). Nearest-sample handles a DST change or a corrected RC 2 clock. The time rules:
- DJI MP4 with moov: the mvhd time.
- DJI photo, set or truncated clip: EXIF DateTimeOriginal (or the filename stamp) minus the offset.
- Non-DJI names (Autel MAX_*, unknown makers): a 'floating' wall clock (mvhd as written, or EXIF, or mtime in the PC zone). LocalDate is its date, with no time zone conversion.
The zone comes from the item's own GPS. Without GPS, it comes from the nearest GPS item on the card within 12 h, otherwise from the PC zone. An Etc/* result (a point over water) is replaced by the PC zone.

components.name: Core/Planning: Newness
components.responsibility:
Pure status rules.
Videos: in the library or the ledger (name + size) means Imported, with its event folder. Same name but a different size means Conflict (not copyable; resolve manually). Anything else is New. A truncated clip (HasMoov = false) is New but unticked, with a 'truncated' badge.
Photos and sets: ledger hit, or name + size (and, for a set, the set name + members) in the photo root, means Imported. Otherwise New if the photo's LocalDate is a date with New videos, or its CaptureUtc is after the watermark. Otherwise ProbablyImported, unticked, with the reason shown. Watermark = max(library DJI stamp minus clock.OffsetNear(stamp), ledger.LastVideoUtc). Today that is 2026-09-27 18:24:16Z.

components.name: Core/Planning: Clusterer
components.responsibility:
Groups videos only; photos go flat and never create folders. Items are taken in (CaptureUtc, Id) order, and a new group starts on any of three rules.
(a) Time: LocalDate gap to the previous item > G days AND Δt > H hours.
(b) Location (the requested radius / big-jump rule): the item has GPS, the group has a centroid (mean of unit vectors, safe across the antimeridian), and the haversine distance is > R km. This fires on the same day or the next day alike.
(c) Existing folders: the item is Imported into library folder F and the group already holds Imported items from a different folder. The user's existing folder boundaries are hard; this replaces the reference design's AppendSplit.
Items without GPS never split a group by location and never move the centroid. There is no power-on-session rule and no re-homing; the user fixes rare no-GPS edge cases with Split or Merge. About 60 lines of code.

components.name: Core/Planning: FolderDecider + FolderNamer
components.responsibility:
Decides each group's target folder.
- No New items: AlreadyImported.
- Holds Imported items from folder F: Append(F), high confidence.
- Otherwise, a library folder F qualifies when F.NameDate ≤ g.Start ≤ F.End + G. A group never goes into a folder named after a later date than its first clip. Then: both locations known and within R (F's location from the ledger centroid, or from leftovers on the card) means Append, high. F's location unknown and the dates overlap (g.Start ≤ F.End) means Append, medium. Only adjacent with location unknown, or more than R away, means NewFolder. When several qualify, pick the smallest date gap.
Naming: a new folder is <videoRoot>\YYYY\YYYY-MM\YYYY-MM-DD <desc>, dated by the start local date, even when the trip crosses into another month or year. Description cleaning: <>:"/\|?* and control characters become spaces, whitespace is collapsed, trailing dots and spaces are trimmed, and the length is capped at 80; commas are kept.
Description suggestions: the existing folder's description when appending, else the description of a ledger place within R, else blank.
Photos go to <photoRoot>\<name>. A set goes to <photoRoot>\<set>\; if that folder name is already taken with different contents, it becomes '<set> YYYY-MM-DD' (proposed default, not yet approved by the user).

components.name: Core/Copy: CopyEngine
components.responsibility:
Copies sequentially, one file at a time.
Preflight: both roots exist; free space on each destination volume ≥ total size + 1 GiB; no destination has the same name with a different size; stale *.uas-sort.tmp files of our own are removed.
Per file:
1. Destination exists with the same size: Skipped (already there), and ledgered.
2. Destination exists with a different size: Failed. Never overwrite.
3. Otherwise read the card sequentially in 1 MiB blocks, hashing with IncrementalHash SHA-256, while writing <dest>.uas-sort.tmp (CreateNew).
4. Flush(true), then copy the source's creation and modified times (File.Copy would reset the creation time).
5. Re-read the tmp file through OpenVerify and compare hashes. This runs before the rename, so the final name only ever holds a verified file, and the .tmp name keeps OneDrive from syncing it mid-check (docs claim, UNVERIFIED).
6. MoveNoOverwrite to the final name, then ledger.Append.
On a hash mismatch: delete the tmp, retry once, then Failed. On cancel: delete the current tmp and stop; completed files stay and are ledgered.

components.name: UasSort.App (WPF shell)
components.responsibility: A single MainWindow with thin view models. It holds no business logic. It adapts DriveInfo.GetDrives() to VolumeInfo, builds GuardedFileOps(RealFileOps), and runs scan and copy on Task.Run with IProgress. The folder pickers use WPF OpenFolderDialog. Every edit goes through PlanEditor and the grid is rebuilt from the returned Plan.

dataFlow:
1. Launch. SettingsStore.Load. If VideoRoot or PhotoRoot is missing or invalid, the header path boxes are highlighted. LedgerStore.Load gives a LedgerSnapshot.
2. Find the card. App: DriveInfo.GetDrives() is mapped to VolumeInfo, then CardLocator.Find picks candidates. The first candidate is selected; Rescan and Browse… are the only other ways in. There are no device-arrival hooks.
3. Scan the card. CardScanner.Scan lists it through GuardedFileOps into a CardInventory of Video, Photo, SetItem, Skipped and Unknown entries.
4. Probe each item, sequentially, on a background task with progress:
   - Video: Mp4Probe.Read on the card stream, giving the mvhd time, HasMoov and GPS.
   - Photo, and each set's first frame: StillProbe.Read, giving the naive DateTimeOriginal and the EXIF GPS position.
   - A probe error is kept on the item and the item falls back to filename/mtime time with no GPS.
5. List the library. IFileOps.List(VideoRoot) and List(PhotoRoot) return names, sizes and mtimes only, which feed LibraryIndex.Build. The guard makes opening any library file impossible.
6. Resolve times. DroneClock.Learn uses the card's DJI MP4s (filename stamp vs mvhd UTC) with the settings offset as fallback. TimeResolver.Resolve then gives each item a CaptureUtc, a TzId (GeoTimeZone from its own GPS, else inherited from the nearest GPS item within 12 h, else the PC zone) and a LocalDate.
7. Classify. Newness.Video first. newVideoDates and the watermark are then derived, and Newness.Photo follows.
8. Group and decide. Clusterer.Cluster on the videos, using the time gap, the GPS radius / big-jump rule and existing-folder boundaries. For each group, FolderDecider.Decide, SuggestDescription and NewFolderPath run. Photos are grouped by LocalDate for display only; their destination is always <photoRoot>\\name, or <photoRoot>\\<set>\\ for a pano or hyperlapse set.
9. Review. The user ticks or unticks items and photo days, edits descriptions, switches New ↔ Append via the dropdown (from AppendCandidates), and uses Merge with previous or Split here. Each edit is a PlanEditor call that returns a new Plan.
10. Copy. PlanEditor.Jobs gives the job list, CopyEngine.Preflight runs, then CopyEngine.RunAsync. Each file is copied to tmp with hashing, flushed, stamped with the source times, re-read and compared, renamed to its final name and ledgered. Progress shows in the footer. Settings.DroneClockOffsetMinutes is updated to the last learned offset.
11. Finish. A summary lists copied, already-there and failed items, plus a 'safe to format?' line. That line says No while any failed item, any unticked New / ProbablyImported / truncated item, or any Unknown file remains. The card is never written.
uiScreens:
A single MainWindow with no wizard and no extra windows, apart from the system folder pickers and one confirmation MessageBox before copying.
Header row: card ComboBox (label + drive letter, with any RC-card warning), Rescan, Browse…; Video root and Photo root path boxes with … buttons, saved immediately. Below it a status line, e.g. '212 files · 15 new videos · 48 new photos · 3 'probably imported' photo days · 1 truncated clip · 2 unknown files'.
Body (scrolling):
- Video groups: one Expander per group. The header has the include checkbox, the date range, a Target ComboBox ('New folder' plus 'Append to 2026-09-27 Zachar Bay' and other candidates, with a medium-confidence badge where it applies), a Description TextBox, and a read-only path preview (…\\2026\\2026-09\\2026-09-27 Zachar Bay\\). It also shows clip count, new count and GB, the centroid (57.542N 153.741W), spread (1.8 km), distance and gap from the previous group (e.g. '54 km, next day' shows why it was split), and a Merge-with-previous button. The body is a DataGrid of clips: include, name, local time, size, lat/lon, km from centroid, status badge (New / Imported / Conflict / Truncated), and a 'Split here' button that splits before that row. Groups that are already fully imported are collapsed and greyed.
- Photos: one DataGrid grouped by local date. Each day row has an include checkbox, a count, and a reason ('new: day has new videos', 'new: after last imported video 2026-09-27 10:24 AKDT', 'probably imported: imported videos exist that day'). Set rows show their destination folder, including any collision suffix. A first-run note appears while the ledger is empty.
- Skipped / Unknown: a collapsed Expander listing Unknown files (never copied) and the counts of skipped files.
Footer: 'Copy 17 files · 9.4 GB (C: 8.1 GB, D: 1.3 GB)', the Copy button, and during a run a ProgressBar (bytes), the current file and Cancel. After a run, a result panel lists failures and the 'safe to format?' verdict. There is no settings dialog; R, G and H live in settings.json. No map, no thumbnails, default light theme.
persistence:
Two files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\\uas-sort\\, kept out of OneDrive:
(1) settings.json: VideoRoot, PhotoRoot, RadiusKm = 25, DayGap = 1, SplitGuardHours = 3, DroneClockOffsetMinutes = -240, the last learned offset. It is written to a temp file and then swapped in with File.Replace.
(2) ledger.jsonl: append-only, one line per verified file, written only after the hash check passes. Fields: v, name, size, kind, set, captureUtc, timeSource, lat, lon, localDate, dest, sha256, copiedUtc. About 250 B per line, so 10k rows is about 2.5 MB and loads in about 120 ms (measured in the stack spike).
A ledger hit (name + size, or for a set its name + members) counts as Imported whether or not the file is still in the library. So files the user culled are not offered again, and there is no separate 'removed from library' status.
Folder GPS for append decisions is derived at load time as the mean of the ledger entries' lat/lon for each destination folder. Nothing else is cached: no plan cache, no thumbnails, no database, no schema migrations. Nothing is ever written to the card. Library writes happen only at commit time: EnsureDirectory for new or year/month folders, <name>.uas-sort.tmp, then a rename to the final name.
errorHandling:
Scan: an unreadable card file becomes an item with Probe.Error. The scan does not stop; the item falls back to filename/mtime time with no GPS, and the reason is shown. If no card is found, an empty state offers Rescan and Browse…. An RC-card candidate shows a warning and imports nothing. If a root is missing (for example D: PhotoEdits unplugged), preflight blocks copying to that root with a clear message; the user can untick photos and still copy videos.
Time sanity: a CaptureUtc before 2015 or later than the PC clock + 1 day gets a 'clock not set' badge showing its time source. When no MP4 on the card has a moov, times use the settings offset and the source says so.
Safety: GuardedFileOps throws UnsafeIoException on any library read, card write or non-tmp delete. It is treated as a bug and stops the operation. This rule is tested.
Copying:
- Destination has the same name with a different size: Failed, never overwritten.
- Same name and size: AlreadyThere, and ledgered.
- Hash mismatch: the tmp is deleted, the file retried once, then Failed.
- IOException (card pulled, disk full): the current tmp is deleted, the rest of the run stops, and the summary lists what completed. Re-running shows completed files as Imported.
- Cancel: the current tmp is deleted and the run stops.
- Leftover *.uas-sort.tmp from a crash: removed at preflight.
- Unbuffered verify read fails: fall back to a buffered re-read, and record that in the report.
Truncated MP4 (no moov): shown New but unticked, with a badge suggesting the user power the drone on with the card in it to let DJI repair the file (UNVERIFIED for the Air 3S), or tick it to copy as-is.
Conflict items cannot be ticked; the user resolves them in Explorer.
End of run: a 'Don't format the card yet' warning while anything New or ProbablyImported is left unticked, anything failed, or any Unknown file exists.
deliberatelyExcluded: Tray icon, background service, auto-start and WM_DEVICECHANGE auto-rescan (you launch the app manually; there is a Rescan button). Reverse geocoding for folder-name suggestions (GeoNames extract, Nominatim), maps and thumbnails (the MP4 tnal/covr covers). Reading .SRT files for GPS, and copying .LRF or .SRT files. Photos could be missed if the user formats the card without looking. Mitigations: day-level ticking, a first-run note, and the 'don't format yet' verdict.

name: uas-sort: an offload app built for data safety (a journal records each step, files are checked before they get their final name, the planning core does no file access)
summary:
uas-sort is a WPF app for .NET 10 LTS that the user launches by hand. All of its decisions come from a planning library that does no file access. That library is a line-for-line C# port of the tested Python reference `spikes/grouping/grouping.py`: its 37 tests pass (re-run 2026-09-27), and replaying the real library with it rebuilds all 8 of the user's folders. The user asked whether EXIF has coordinates. Yes, it does:
- DNGs carry EXIF GPS. MetadataExtractor reads PANO_0001.DNG as 57.799648, -152.390180.
- MP4s have no EXIF GPS. Their coordinates come from the first sample of the djmd telemetry track. That reader matches exiftool exactly while reading only about 2 KB of the file.
- Grouping therefore joins consecutive local days (G = 1 day) and starts a new group when a clip is more than R = 25 km from the group's centre. That one rule covers both the user's "radius around where they're taken" and "a big jump, even on the next day". For example, Council Road and Anvil Mountain are 53 km apart on consecutive days and get split. Photo coordinates attach photos to groups and give the time zone of the shoot location.

Every copy goes through one write path that can neither overwrite a file nor delete one it didn't create:
1. Record the step in a journal first.
2. Copy to a hidden .tmp file in the destination folder, hashing as it copies.
3. Flush the file to disk.
4. Read it back with Windows caching bypassed, so the check hits the disk.
5. Only then rename it to its final name, without replacing anything.

So a file with its final name always has verified content. OneDrive never uploads a partial file. A crash or pulled card can be recovered by comparing the journal, the destination folder and the card. Each run ends with a check of the card that sorts every card file into one of these: verified by hash, matched by name and size, only "probably imported" by the photo rule, or not accounted for.

components.name: Ports: typed time values and file-system interfaces (UasSort.Domain.Abstractions)
components.responsibility:
Defines the only ways the core can touch the outside world. Each interface is shaped so an unsafe action cannot even be written.

Typed time values:
- UtcInstant, which always has Kind=Utc.
- NaiveStamp, for drone-clock and EXIF wall-clock stamps. It has no time zone and cannot be converted without an offset resolution.
- SiteZone: the IANA ID, the source (GPS, inherited or PC), any alternative zones, and IsEtc.
- DateOnly LocalDate.

These types mean a drone-clock stamp cannot be treated as UTC by accident.

The interfaces IClock, ITimeZoneResolver and IPlaceNamer are injected. The domain project bans DateTime.Now, TimeZoneInfo.Local and all of System.IO.

components.name: Win32 adapters (UasSort.Platform.Windows)
components.responsibility:
The only project that touches the real file system and Win32. It contains the real implementations of the ports plus these Windows-specific pieces:
- A volume scanner that finds cards.
- A power guard that keeps the PC awake during a copy.
- A single-instance guard.
- An optional hook that rescans when a device is plugged in.
- The GeoTimeZone-based time zone resolver.

It is the one place allowed to call File.Delete, and it does so only inside DeleteOwnTemp, with a guard on the name pattern.

Checked 2026-09-27: listing the cloud-only Kodiak folder with Get-ChildItem and [IO.File]::GetAttributes left every file at 0x401620, so listing does not trigger a download.

Turns a raw card listing into units to be copied, and never drops anything silently.

- It accepts every DCIM media folder, not just DJI_001.
- It recognises the DJI name pattern, including custom suffixes: ^DJI_(\d{14})_(\d{4})_([A-Z])(?:_[^.]*)?\.(\w+)$.
- It pairs a JPG with a DNG of the same base name into one PhotoUnit.
- It treats PANORAMA/<set> and HYPERLAPSE/<set> as one PhotoSetUnit each.
- It marks a video with a sibling .<name>.MP4.trinf file as a probable unfinished recording.
- Files it deliberately skips carry the rule that skipped them.
- Any other file under DCIM becomes UnknownEntry, which must be ticked to copy or ignored explicitly.

components.name: MediaProbe (UasSort.Media)
components.responsibility:
Reads the minimum needed from card files and turns it into facts. It reads about 2–4 KB per MP4, about 100 KB per DNG, and only the first frame of a pano or hyperlapse set.

**MP4 layout.** A lazy box walker:
- Handles 64-bit box sizes, size 0 (box runs to end of file) and uuid boxes.
- Never reads mdat, and never reads moov whole.
- Reports health: Ok, NoMoov, BoxOverrun or Fragmented.

**djmd reader.** Reads the protocol, drone serial, power-on uptime, and the first and last GPS fix, looking fields up by protocol.
- If the first sample has no fix, it probes samples 0–9, then powers of two, then the last sample.
- For a file with no moov it falls back to the start of mdat (offset 512).

**EXIF reader.** Uses MetadataExtractor. DateTimeOriginal is taken from the ExifDirectoryBase that actually contains that tag; this avoids the DNG pitfall of reading the raw-image sub-IFD, which has no date. GPS comes from GpsDirectory.TryGetGeoLocation.

**SRT reader** (optional): latitude and longitude from the first caption, if an SRT exists.

components.name: DroneClockModel and TimeNormalizer (Domain)
components.responsibility:
Gives every item a capture time in UTC and the local calendar date at the shoot location, with the source of each value recorded.

**Capture time, first rule that applies:**
1. The MP4 creation time (true UTC).
2. A real GPS time (the Air 3S never has one).
3. EXIF DateTimeOriginal plus OffsetTimeOriginal.
4. The drone-clock stamp (EXIF date, else file name) minus the learned offset: from the nearest MP4 sample on the card within 60 days, else the card's most common offset, else the saved offset setting (currently −4 h).
5. Autel videos: the creation time taken as a local wall clock with no zone.
6. Autel photos or unknown makers: the file time, as a local wall clock.
7. Otherwise the file time.

**Shoot-location time zone.** Found from GPS. An item without GPS takes it from a GPS item in the same power-on session, else from the nearest GPS item within 12 h, else from the PC's zone.

**LocalDate** is the wall-clock date for Autel items, otherwise the UTC capture time converted to the shoot-location zone.

**Flags DateNeedsReview when:**
- the zone is an Etc/ ocean zone;
- the lookup returned alternative zones and the local time is within an hour of midnight;
- the capture time is before 2015 or more than one day ahead of the PC clock.

components.name: LibraryIndex (Domain)
components.responsibility:
Builds all knowledge of the library from file names, sizes, file times and attributes, plus the ledger. It never reads library file content.

**Lookups**
- By name and size, case-insensitive, across the video root and the photo root.
- By name alone, to find conflicts.
- By size alone, for files of 1 MiB or more, to find possible renamed duplicates.

**Event folders.** The nearest folder above a file, at any depth, named `YYYY-MM-DD [description]`. The photo-root subtree is excluded even though it currently sits inside the video root (UAS Videos\Picture Offload).

**Folder date ranges.** Built from the name date plus each DJI file-name stamp minus the offset, cross-checked against the file time. If they disagree by more than 2 h, the file time wins and the folder is flagged.

**Folder locations.** From the ledger first, then from card files that are already in the library (read from the card, then saved to the ledger), otherwise unknown. An opt-in setting, off by default, would instead read djmd sample 0 of library files that are stored locally (not cloud-only).

**Watermark.** The start time of the latest imported video; today that is 2026-09-27T18:24:16Z.

components.name: NewnessClassifier (Domain)
components.responsibility:
Decides exactly which items are new. Every status carries a reason code that the interface and the tests both use.

**Videos, first match wins**
1. IgnoredByUser.
2. Imported: name and size found in the library.
3. RemovedFromLibrary: in the ledger but gone from the library.
4. Conflict: same name, different size. The library copy may be truncated. Never overwritten.
5. PossibleDuplicate: same size (1 MiB or more) under a different name.
6. New.

**Photos** (the user's rule)
- Imported: found in the ledger, or name and size found in the photo root.
- New (AfterWatermark): taken after the watermark.
- New (SameDayAsNewVideo): on a local date that has new videos.
- Otherwise ProbablyImported, either ImportedVideosThatDay or PhotoOnlyDayBeforeWatermark.

**Pano and hyperlapse sets** count as imported only if the set folder name and every member's name and size match. PANO_000N names repeat across sets.

components.name: Clusterer and PhotoAttacher (Domain)
components.responsibility:
Builds the proposed groups from time and location. Only videos set group boundaries.

**Time split.** A clip starts a new group when its local date is more than G days after the previous item and more than H hours have passed.

**Location split** (this rule covers both the "radius" and the "big jump" the user asked for). A clip starts a new group when all of these hold:
- it has GPS;
- the group has a centre, computed as the mean of unit vectors;
- its power-on session is not the session of any group member that has GPS (this restriction to GPS members is the regression fix found in the spike);
- its haversine distance from the centre is more than R.

**Clips without GPS** never cause a location split. When a location split happens, trailing clips without GPS move with their power-on session, or otherwise to whichever side is nearer in time.

**Photos** attach to the video group nearest in time, within ±1 local day and within R. Photos left over form PhotosOnly groups, which are display-only.

Every boundary records its reason, for example `SplitReason.Distance(53.2 km)`.

The replay shows the defaults are robust: any R from 12.5 to 53 km and any G from 1 to 11 days reproduce all 8 folders.

components.name: AppendDecider, FolderNamer and DescriptionSuggester (Domain)
components.responsibility:
Chooses where each video group goes and what the new folder is called.

**Decisions**
- AlreadyImported: the group has no new clips.
- Append(F, High): the group contains imported clips from folder F.
- AppendSplit: imported clips from several folders; each new clip goes to the folder of its nearest-in-time imported neighbour.
- Append(F, High or Medium): F's name date ≤ group start ≤ F's end + G days, and the two are within R. It is Medium when one location is unknown and the dates overlap.
- NewFolder: dates only adjacent and a location unknown (the dropdown still offers the append), or no suitable folder.
- Clips are **never** appended to a folder whose name date is after them.

**New folder path.** `<videoRoot>\YYYY\YYYY-MM\YYYY-MM-DD <desc>`, dated by the local date of the earliest new clip.

**Cleaning the description**
- Replace `<>:"/\|?*` and control characters with a space.
- Collapse runs of whitespace and trim.
- Remove trailing dots.
- Limit to 80 characters.
- Keep commas (as in "Newport, RI").

**Suggestions, in order**
1. The existing folder's description, when appending.
2. A description used before for a ledger folder within R.
3. From GeoNames: a named feature within about 2–5 km, or "near <town>" within about 50 km.
4. Blank, which requires the user to type one.

Builds the offload plan and applies the user's edits to it, with undo. Edits are pure functions that return a new plan, and Decide re-runs on every group an edit touches.

**Destinations**

components.name: PlanValidator (Domain): the safety check before copying
components.responsibility:
Runs on every edit and runs again right before copying, against a fresh library listing and a fresh stat of each card file (to catch anything that changed in between).

**Blocking errors**
- Two operations with the same final path (case-insensitive).
- A final path that already exists and was not an explicit keep-both.
- A destination on a card or source volume.
- A destination outside the configured roots.
- A video in a new folder whose local date is before the folder's date.
- A new folder whose date is not the group's start local date.
- An included item with an unresolved DateNeedsReview flag.
- Invalid characters, or a path longer than 32k characters.
- A root that can't be reached (for example, D: unplugged).
- Not enough free space on a destination volume. The margin is the larger of 2 GB and 5%.
- A card file whose size or file time changed since the scan (2 s tolerance).

**Warnings** (shown on the confirmation screen)
- A truncated MP4 (no moov, or a .trinf sibling).
- ProbablyImported photos left unticked.
- Unknown files.
- A photo root nested inside the video root.

components.name: CopyExecutor and VerifiedFileCopier (UasSort.Transfer)
components.responsibility:
Copies files one at a time, in plan order. Each step is written to the journal (and flushed to disk) before it happens.

**Steps for each file**
1. Stat the card file. If its size or file time changed, fail with SourceChanged.
2. Create any missing folders and record DIR_CREATED for each.
3. Record OP_STARTED with the temp path.
4. Stream the card file into the temp file in 1 MiB buffers, preallocated, hashing with XxHash128 as it goes.
5. Flush the temp file to disk.
6. Copy the creation and write times from the card file.
7. Read the temp file back with Windows caching bypassed. The hash must match.
8. For MP4s, run the structure probe on the temp file. It must match the card file: moov present, creation time, first GPS fix. This catches truncation.
9. Record VERIFIED with the hash.
10. Rename to the final name without replacing anything.
11. Record COMMITTED.
12. Add the ledger record and flush it.
13. Record LEDGERED.

**Why the order matters**
- A file with its final name therefore always has verified content.
- The .tmp name stays out of OneDrive's upload (per Microsoft's docs).
- Lightroom never sees a partial file.

**Optional check.** A "paranoid" setting re-reads the card file and compares the hash.

**When the target already exists at rename time**
- If its size and hash match (hashing only files stored locally): mark AlreadyPresent and delete our temp file.
- Otherwise: mark Conflict and delete our temp file.

**Failures**
- A lost card, a full destination or an unreachable destination pauses the whole run.
- Any other failure deletes our temp file and moves on to the next file.
- Cancel lets the current file finish its clean-up first.

components.name: Journal (UasSort.Transfer)
components.responsibility:
A write-ahead record for each copy session, stored in an append-only JSON Lines file.

- **First line:** the whole FrozenPlan: schema version, app version, a snapshot of the settings, the source volume identities and fingerprints, and all operations.
- **Following lines:** one event each, flushed to disk before the action it describes.
- **Last line:** SESSION_CLOSED, with a summary.

The reader ignores a torn final line and reports every other malformed line. Journals are small and are kept, which also gives an audit trail.

components.name: Ledger (UasSort.Transfer)
components.responsibility:
The app's own long-term memory, independent of where files currently sit.

**Record types**
- FileOffloaded: name, size, xxh128, kind, capture time and its source, the naive stamp, zone, local date, GPS (latitude, longitude, altitude), power-on session, drone serial, source volume and card path, destination root kind, root path at the time, destination path, time verified, and flags.
- FolderUpdated: path, description, centre, date range.
- FolderLocationLearned.
- IgnoreForever: name and size.

**How it is written and read**
- One writer. The file is opened with FileShare.Read, and every record is flushed to disk.
- Loading removes duplicate records (same name, size and hash).
- Loading tolerates a torn last line.
- A malformed line elsewhere is reported, and the file is never rewritten in place.
- When a session closes, the ledger is copied to a rolling ledger.jsonl.bak. It can also be copied to a backup folder the user chooses.

components.name: RecoveryService (UasSort.Transfer)
components.responsibility:
Runs at every launch. It finds sessions with no SESSION_CLOSED line and rebuilds the true state of each file from the last journal event, whether the temp file exists, and whether the final file exists and its size.

**Rules**
- **Final file present and VERIFIED recorded:** hash the final file (it is local) against the journal hash, then add any missing ledger record.
- **Temp file present:** DeleteOwnTemp, then queue the file again.
- **OP_STARTED recorded but no temp file:** queue the file again.
- **Final file present but VERIFIED never recorded** (should not happen under this protocol): mark it Suspect. Verify it against the card if the card's fingerprint matches; otherwise leave it untouched and flag it.
- **Empty folders this session created:** removed only on "Discard".

**When the card must match.** Resuming requires the same source volume: the same volume serial, and the planned files still present with the same size and file time. A different or reformatted card cannot resume; the session can only be closed after clean-up.
components.interface:
IReadOnlyList<IncompleteSession> FindIncomplete()
RecoveryPlan Reconcile(IncompleteSession s, IReadOnlyList<ISourceVolume> present, IDestinationFs fs)
RunResult Apply(RecoveryPlan rp, ...)
    // Apply then continues with CopyExecutor on the operations queued again

components.name: CardAuditor (UasSort.Transfer)
components.responsibility:
Answers "Is everything on this card backed up?" honestly, file by file.

**Each card file is accounted for by exactly one of:**
- HashVerifiedThisRun
- LedgerHash: verified in an earlier run
- LibraryNameSize: matched by name and size only, content not compared
- ProbablyImportedHeuristic
- IgnoredByUser
- SkippedByRule: expected non-media, such as MISC, LRF or trinf files

Anything else is **Unaccounted**.

**Verdict.** "All media backed up" only when nothing is Unaccounted, nothing is only heuristic, and every truncated clip has been acknowledged. The app never formats or deletes, so this is advice only.

components.name: App shell (UasSort.App, WPF plus CommunityToolkit.Mvvm)
components.responsibility:
The composition root and user interface. The views contain no logic.

MainViewModel is a state machine: Startup → Recovery (if needed) → SelectCard → Scanning → Review → Confirm → Copying → Results.

ReviewViewModel wraps PlanEditor with undo and redo, and saves a draft of the edits so a crash doesn't lose them. Background work runs on Task.Run with cancellation, and progress is reported through IProgress.

Thumbnails are the 160×90 JPEG already inside each DJI MP4, read from the card; no video is decoded.

components.responsibility: A console front end over the same composition root. It lets the plan be checked on a real card without the interface, and supports a rehearsal run that copies into scratch roots before the first real offload.

dataFlow:
**1. Launch**
- SingleInstanceGuard makes sure only one copy is running.
- Load settings.json and the ledger.
- RecoveryService.FindIncomplete. If there is an interrupted session, show the Recovery screen before anything else.

**2. Choose the source**
- VolumeScanner lists candidate cards.
- The user picks one or more volumes. A drone connected by USB can show both InternalStorage and SD_card, and both should be offloaded together.

**3. Scan (read-only)**
- Enumerate the card, then CardClassifier.Classify.
- Run MediaProbe on each unit, one after another: about 2–4 KB per MP4 in 5–16 ms; about 94 KB per DNG.
- Win32LibraryLister lists the video root and the photo root: names, sizes, file times and attributes only. Checked: listing does not trigger downloads.
- Load the ledger snapshot.

**4. Normalize**
- Learn the drone-clock offset from the MP4s on the card: file-name stamp minus creation time. All 7 DJI library folders measured −4.0 h.
- Run TimeNormalizer on each item: capture time in UTC, shoot-location zone (GPS, inherited or PC), local date, review flags.
- Worked example: Zachar Bay 0128 has file stamp 2026-09-27 14:06:27 on the drone clock and creation time 18:06:27Z. Its GPS gives America/Anchorage, so the local date is 2026-09-27.

**5. Build the plan**
- Build the LibraryIndex, then learn library folder locations from card files that are already in the library.
- Classify videos, then collect the dates that have new videos, then compute the watermark, then classify photos.
- Cluster the videos (G = 1 day, R = 25 km, H = 3 h), attach photos, then Decide for each group.
- Destinations come from DestinationResolver. Description suggestions come from the ledger, then GeoNames.

**6. Review**
- The user splits, merges, renames, re-targets and ticks items. Each edit is a pure PlanEditor.Apply followed by PlanValidator.Validate (on in-memory data), so the interface always shows the exact final paths and any blocking problems.

**7. Confirm**
- Freeze the plan.
- Re-list the target folders and re-stat each card file, then validate again. Any blocking problem sends the user back to Review.
- The screen shows the number of files, bytes and free space after copying for each destination volume.

**8. Execute**
- PowerGuard keeps the PC awake.
- Write the journal header.
- CopyExecutor copies each file in turn: verified temp copy, then rename with no replace, then ledger record.

**9. Finish**
- Write FolderUpdated and FolderLocationLearned records to the ledger.
- CardAuditor produces the verdict.
- Write SESSION_CLOSED to the journal and back up the ledger.
- Show the Results screen, with "Open folder" buttons.

**Where coordinates come from**

| Source | Used for |
|---|---|
| MP4 djmd first fix (last fix used to catch a stale first fix) | Clustering, zone, folder location |
| DNG/JPG EXIF GPS | Attaching photos, photo-only groups, zone for photo local dates, place-name suggestions |
| Pano or hyperlapse set, first frame's EXIF GPS | The same as a single photo |
| SRT first caption, if present | Fallback |

**What never happens**
- No file is ever opened for writing on a source volume.
- No library file is ever opened, except a file this session just committed. That exception applies only during recovery re-hashing and only after IsCloudOnly is checked as false.
uiScreens:
**1. Recovery**
- Shown only if a session was interrupted.
- One row per file with its state: done, temp file left, needs recopy, or suspect.
- A card-match indicator.
- Buttons: "Resume" (only when the same card is present) and "Discard temp files and close session", which deletes only the journal-listed .tmp files and empty folders this session created.

**2. Select card**
- Each detected volume shows its label, serial, file system, DCIM folders, and counts of videos, photos and sets.
- An RC 2 card shows a warning instead.
- Rescan, and "Browse to folder…".
- A banner when a root can't be reached, for example D: unplugged.

**3. Scanning**
- Progress for listing the card, probing media and listing the library, with Cancel.

**4. Review**
- **Left pane:** the list of groups.
  - Video groups show the date range (local), the place suggestion, clip count and size, and a decision badge: New folder, Append to "2026-09-27 Zachar Bay" (high or medium), Already imported, or Needs review.
  - A split-reason chip, such as "54 km from previous group" or "3-day gap".
  - PhotosOnly groups appear in a separate section.
- **Right pane:** details for the selected group.
  - An editable description with a suggestion dropdown.
  - A target dropdown: New folder, or Append to an existing folder, with the matching folders listed.
  - A live preview of the final path.
  - A grid of members: thumbnail, name, local time and zone (with source), distance from the group centre, status and reason, and an include checkbox.
  - Photos are grouped by day, with the reason and an "include whole day" link.
  - Warning icons for truncated files, conflicts, and dates needing review.
- **Actions:** Split here, Merge with previous or next, Move to group, Ignore forever, Undo and Redo.
- **Bottom bar:** blocking problems and warnings from the validator. Continue stays disabled while any problem is blocking.

**5. Confirm**
- For each destination volume: files, bytes, and free space before and after.
- The new folders that will be created and the existing folders that will get files.
- The warning list.
- A button to export the dry-run plan as JSON.
- "Copy N files (X GB)".

**6. Copying**
- The current file's progress and its stage: copying, flushing, verifying, committing.
- Overall bytes and speed, and an estimated time remaining.
- Failures listed as they happen.
- Pause and Cancel, where Cancel lets the current file finish its clean-up first.
- A "PC will stay awake" indicator.
- A red "reinsert the card" pause state.

**7. Results / card audit**
- Counts in each accounting category.
- A verdict line, for example: "All 142 media files on this card are backed up (97 hash-verified, 45 matched by name+size)", or "12 photos are only probably imported — don't format yet".
- The list of unaccounted files.
- Open-folder buttons.

**8. Settings**
- The video root and photo root.
- R, G and H for grouping.
- The drone-clock fallback offset.
- The JPG pairing policy, and the policies for set-folder and flat-photo name collisions.
- Paranoid source re-read (on or off).
- An opt-in read of locally stored library files to learn folder locations.
- The ledger backup folder.
- Rehearsal mode, which sends copies to scratch roots.
persistence:
Everything lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\uas-sort\, outside OneDrive. Nothing is ever written to the card.

**settings.json**
- Holds a schema version, the two roots, the grouping settings, the offset fallback (last learned value −4 h), the policies, the verify mode, the backup folder and a rehearsal flag.
- Saved by writing settings.json.tmp, flushing it to disk, then File.Replace with a backup.

**ledger.jsonl**
- Append-only, one JSON record per line with a schema version and a record ID. Flushed to disk after every record.
- Plus a rolling ledger.jsonl.bak, and an optional copy in a backup folder the user chooses.
- This is the long-term truth about photos, folder locations and date ranges, and "ignore forever" choices. For videos the library listing stays the primary truth, and the ledger only adds detail.

**Session journals**
- `sessions\<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>_<sessionId>.journal.jsonl`: the frozen plan followed by write-ahead events. Kept indefinitely; they are tiny.

**Drafts**
- `drafts\<card fingerprint>.json`: in-progress Review edits, deleted when the plan is frozen.

**Logs**
- `logs\uas-sort-<date>.log`: plain text, a small built-in writer, rotated after 30 days.

**GeoNames extract**
- Embedded in the app as a resource, so nothing is written for it.

**Temp files during a copy**
- `<final directory>\<name>.<sessionTag8>.uas-sort.tmp`, with the Hidden attribute set. It exists only between the start of a copy and its rename, and only journal-listed temp files are ever deleted.

**Data kept in the library itself:** none. No manifests or sidecars are added to the user's folders. This follows the no-content-reading rule and keeps the library clean. Whether to also snapshot the ledger into the library is an open decision for the user.
errorHandling:
**Principle:** no failure ever overwrites, moves or deletes the user's data. The only files the app deletes are its own journal-listed .tmp files and empty folders the journal says this session created.

**Card removed**
- **During the scan:** abort the scan, write nothing, and ask the user to rescan.
- **During a copy:** the read fails with an IOException, so the temp file is deleted and the run pauses with "Reinsert card".
  - The app matches the card by volume serial, then by checking the planned files' sizes and file times.
  - Resume continues from the journal. A different card cannot resume.

**App crash or power loss at any point**
- Handled by RecoveryService at the next launch, which uses the state table in its component description.
- If the crash lands between the rename and the ledger write, the final file still exists. The library listing therefore reports it as Imported anyway, and recovery adds the missing ledger record.

**Destination problems**
- **Full, or unreachable (D: unplugged, OneDrive folder missing):** delete the temp file and pause the run. Free space is checked before the run starts, with a margin.
- **Hash mismatch when reading back:** delete the temp file and copy once more. A second mismatch marks the file Failed(VerifyMismatch) and warns about a possible reader or card fault.
- **MP4 structure differs from the card file:** treated the same as a hash mismatch.

**Target already exists at rename time**
- The rename fails with 0x800700B7, never overwrites, and the file becomes AlreadyPresent or Conflict (see CopyExecutor).

**Card file changed between the scan and the copy**
- SourceChanged: skip the file and report it.

**Truncated recording (no moov, or a .trinf sibling)**
- It is still copied by default, because it is real footage, and is flagged in the interface and the ledger.
- The audit suggests powering the drone on with the card inserted to repair it before formatting.
- If a repaired, larger version turns up later, it is a Conflict, with a "keep both" option. The broken library copy is never replaced automatically.

**Clock and time zone doubts**
- A capture time before 2015 or in the future, an Etc/ ocean zone, or alternative zones near midnight set DateNeedsReview. That blocks the group until the user confirms or changes the date.
- If the drone-clock offset can't be resolved, the file time is used and flagged.

**Library files stored only in the cloud**
- They are never opened. IDestinationFs.OpenReadUnbuffered refuses them.
- If a folder's location is unknown because its files are cloud-only, the decision confidence is lowered to Medium or it becomes NewFolder with an append offer.

**Damaged ledger**
- A torn last line is ignored.
- Other bad lines are reported and ignored. They are never rewritten automatically.
- Newness then falls back to the library listing. This can only cause re-offers that the rename-with-no-replace rule makes harmless.

**Unknown file types under DCIM**
- Shown for review and counted as Unaccounted until the user ticks them or ignores them.

**Photo root inside the video root (the current setup)**
- Supported: that subtree is excluded from event folders.
- A photo root on the card volume is a blocking error.

**Second instance of the app**
- Refused with a message, so two instances can never write at once.

**Long paths**
- Handled through the longPathAware manifest. The validator also enforces the limit.

**PC sleep during a copy**
- Prevented by PowerGuard.

**Every error**
- Logged with its operation ID.
- Shown in the interface with the file name, a plain-language cause and the action taken.
deliberatelyExcluded:
- **Background running:** no tray icon, service or auto-launch when a card is inserted. The user launches the app by hand; the optional WM_DEVICECHANGE hook only rescans while the app is open.
- **Changing the card:** no delete, move or format, and no "free up space" option. The card is also never repaired; repairing a truncated MP4 is left to the drone or to djifix/untrunc.
- **Changing library files:** no overwriting or replacing, and no renaming, moving or re-describing of existing library folders or files. Any clean-up is manual.
- **Reading library content:** never, except the opt-in read of locally stored files for folder locations, which is off by default.
- **Lightroom:** no access to the Lightroom catalog (D:\LR_Catalog) and no launching of Lightroom.
- **Metadata tools and writing:** ExifTool is not bundled, and no metadata is ever written into files.
- **Online and map features:** no online reverse geocoding by default (Nominatim is an optional button, one cached request per group), and no map view (tile licensing, and it needs a connection).
- **Other file types:** LRF, SRT and MISC files are not copied. SRT files are only read for GPS.
- **Other features left out:** transcoding or decoding video, parallel copying from several cards, a SQLite database, checking the OneDrive cloud quota, and the auto-re-merge of A-B-A same-day visits (the user merges by hand).
- **Deeper Autel support:** limited to wall-clock dates.
- **Enterprise and multi-camera suffixes:** _W, _Z and _T are accepted but get no special handling.
risks:
**Main risks**

1. **Photo newness is a heuristic.**
   - Photos on days whose videos were already imported, or photo-only days before the watermark, are only "probably imported". On the first run almost every DNG from before 2026-09-27 18:24Z falls into this bucket, because the photo root holds no 2026 DNGs except the pano set.
   - Formatting the card could then lose photos. Mitigations: the card audit refuses the "backed up" verdict, a first-run banner, "include whole day", and the ledger makes this go away once the app is in use.
   - Lightroom may be moving files out of the photo root (for example Auto Import), which is UNVERIFIED. If so, name-and-size matching there never works, and the ledger is the only record. Verifying before the rename also keeps a watched folder from ever seeing a partial file.
2. **Drone clock and exFAT times (UNVERIFIED).** It is unknown whether the drone clock follows Eastern daylight saving (UTC−5 in winter) or stays at UTC−4, and whether exFAT file times on the card are true UTC. Mitigations: the offset comes from the nearest MP4 sample on the card, and the time source is shown. The user should also fix the RC 2's time zone setting.
3. **Time zone lookup limits.** GeoTimeZone's boundary data is from 2025b. It returns Etc/ zones over water, and results can be an hour off near borders. Mitigation: DateNeedsReview, and the land zone of the group or the nearest place is used for ocean points.
4. **Kodiak's location is unknown.** All 30 Kodiak files are cloud-only, so appends to that folder are Medium confidence or NewFolder with an append offer. If the Kodiak road system is more than 25 km across, a future Kodiak trip could split into several groups; the user merges them.
5. **OneDrive behaviour.** The .tmp upload exclusion is known from Microsoft's docs only, not tested here. OneDrive may lock a newly renamed file while uploading it; verifying before the rename avoids the need to read it back afterwards.
6. **exFAT on D: has no journaling.** Power loss can corrupt folder entries. Mitigations: flush to disk plus WRITE_THROUGH renames, and recovery re-hashes files.
7. **Pano and hyperlapse set names repeat after formatting the card.** The collision suffix format still needs the user's decision.
8. **Tooling immaturity.** .NET 10 is not installed on Windows yet (only SDK 9.0.316). WPF's Fluent dark theme is still being developed. FsCheck.Xunit's compatibility with xunit.v3 4.x is UNVERIFIED.
9. **Reader faults that the check can't see.** The hash proves the destination equals the bytes read from the card, not that those bytes were right. Paranoid mode covers this at twice the card read time.
10. **Test fixtures hold personal data.** The sparse fixtures and replay data contain the user's coordinates and drone serial number. Whether they can go in the repo needs the user's decision.
11. **Complexity.** A journal, recovery and a crash-test matrix are more code than a simple copy loop. That is deliberate under this design's data-safety priority; the crash-test matrix is what makes it trustworthy.

**Context facts corrected by the spikes**
- Zachar Bay has 13 MP4s, not 15.
- Kodiak's first clip was 5/22 at 21:52 AKDT, not 17:52. The folder date is unchanged.

**Open decisions for the user**
- The collision suffix format for repeated pano or hyperlapse set names.
- The opt-in read of locally stored library files for folder locations.
- Whether to cap how many days one group can span.
- The default action for a Conflict: skip, or keep both.
- Whether to snapshot the ledger into OneDrive.
- The JPG pairing policy.
- Whether fixtures containing the user's GPS and drone serial may be committed to the repo.

name: uas-sort: a review-first Plan / Review / Commit architecture
summary: The review screen is the product, and everything behind it exists to make that screen fast, honest and reversible. Scanning a card has no side effects and produces one immutable Plan. The Plan holds items, video groups, photo attachments, and the "boundaries" between groups. Each boundary records why it exists: a date gap in days, or a GPS jump in km (for example "54 km jump, 21 h"). The screen draws those boundaries as one-click Merge chips. The user edits the Plan with small typed commands: Merge, Split, MoveItems, Rename, Retarget, SetIncluded. A pure Planner re-derives decisions after each command. The Python reference runs its 37 tests in 5 ms, so recomputing on every edit is cheap, and full undo/redo comes free. Nothing touches disk until one Offload button compiles the Plan into copy jobs. The copy engine copies, verifies each file before it gets its final name, and appends to a ledger after every file. The run ends with an explicit "safe to format this card?" verdict. The engineering is five UI-free net10.0 libraries (Core, Media, Geo, Platform, Review) and a thin WPF shell. Every file-system touchpoint goes behind a narrow port, so the whole flow, including "never read OneDrive placeholder content", can be tested with an in-memory fake file system.

**Framework and target**
- .NET 10 LTS (SDK 10.0.401, runtime 10.0.12). It must be installed on Windows first: the machine has only SDK 9.0.316, and .NET 8 and 9 reach end of support on 2026-11-10.
- Every library targets net10.0 and builds and tests in WSL with the Linux SDK. The shell is UasSort.App, targeting net10.0-windows (WPF).
- Deploy as a framework-dependent single-file exe. The spike measured about 4.9 MB before the map; Mapsui and SkiaSharp native files add more (size UNVERIFIED).

**Packages**

**Data**

**Custom code, no packages**

A pure port of spike D's grouping.py (Normalize, ClassifyVideo, ClassifyPhoto, Cluster, AttachPhotos, Decide) plus Boundary and Reason generation. It is deterministic and has no I/O.

components.name: UasSort.Platform
components.responsibility:
The real Windows implementations of the ports.

**Library listing (WindowsDirectoryLister):**
- Uses FileSystemEnumerable and FileSystemEntry. Attributes, length and mtime come from the directory listing, with no per-file open.
- Spike D verified that listing does not download (hydrate) cloud-only files.

**PlaceholderGuard:**
- Treats a file as unsafe to read when any of these bits is set: 0x400000 (RecallOnDataAccess), 0x40000 (RecallOnOpen) or 0x1000 (Offline).
- **Fails closed off Windows:** WSL shows 0x80 for everything, so it always answers "unsafe" there.

**WindowsFileOps:**
- FileStreamOptions with PreallocationSize.
- The unbuffered read uses FILE_FLAG_NO_BUFFERING (0x20000000) with File.OpenHandle, RandomAccess.Read and 4096-aligned NativeMemory. It falls back to a buffered read if that fails.

**Other pieces:**
- VolumeProvider built on DriveInfo, plus the volume serial.
- JSON stores in %LOCALAPPDATA%\uas-sort.

components.name: UasSort.Review (view models, UI-framework-free)
components.responsibility:
All screen logic lives here, so it can be tested on Linux. These classes know nothing about WPF types.
- Thumbnails are exposed as ReadOnlyMemory<byte>.
- The map is exposed as plain layer data: points, radius circles, jump lines and labels.
- The dispatcher, dialogs and shell launching sit behind interfaces.
- The view models own screen state, selection sync between the map and the grid, keyboard commands, the rules that enable or disable the Offload button, and the issues list.

components.name: UasSort.App (WPF shell)
components.responsibility:
XAML views, and adapters that turn view-model data into WPF objects. It is also the composition root.
- **Views:** a single MainWindow with ThemeMode="System", switching between CardView, ReviewView, OffloadView and SummaryView.
- **MapPanel:** a Mapsui MapControl.
  - Online mode uses OpenStreetMap.CreateTileLayer("uas-sort/1.0 (+contact)") with a persistent tile cache kept at least 7 days, and the attribution always visible.
  - Offline mode needs no tiles. It shows points, R circles, jump lines, a scale bar, and GeoNames labels from PlaceIndex.InBox.
- **Thumbnails:** JpegBytesToBitmapConverter decodes with DecodePixelWidth, backed by an LRU cache of about 400 images. It is used inside a virtualized ItemsControl and DataGrid.
- **Card arrival:** a DeviceWatcher hooks HwndSource for WM_DEVICECHANGE (DBT_DEVICEARRIVAL, DBT_DEVTYP_VOLUME), then waits about 1.5 s and rescans (UNVERIFIED, since no card was available). The Rescan button is always there.
- **Keyboard:** input bindings.

App.xaml.cs composes: Settings, Ledger, VolumeProvider, Lister, FileSource, Probes, GeoTimeZoneResolver, PlaceIndex, Planner, PlanSession, CopyEngine, then the view models.

components.name: UasSort.Cli (developer harness)
components.responsibility:
Headless use of the same Core, Media and Geo code.
- `plan`: a dry run against a real card or folder. It prints groups, boundaries and decisions as a table or JSON, and writes nothing.
- `replay`: replays the library listing, as in spike D.
- `make-fake-card`: writes a synthetic DCIM tree (built with SyntheticMp4Builder) into a temp folder, so the WPF app can be driven without a real card.
